basis: Inherited carcinoma arising in renal tubular cells; additional organs depend on the specific hereditary syndrome.
Vertebral segmentation defects, rib fusion, scoliosis and joint contractures define the skeletal disorder.
Inborn deglycosylation disorder; substantial neurodevelopmental impairment is a major feature across subtypes. Hepatic and lacrimal findings vary by subtype.
Hepatitis B virus infects the liver; extrahepatic damaging manifestations are uncommon.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; persistent bowel dysfunction in 3/3 and joint contractures in 2/3 support involvement. Fine/sparse hair is a dysmorphic feature.
An isolated dystonic movement disorder; laryngeal and limb dystonia reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than separate airway or muscle disease.
CRYGD-associated cataract directly affects the ocular lens.
Isolated androgenetic hair loss; androgen sensitivity does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Plasma cell neoplasm without marrow involvement; roughly 80% arise in upper respiratory sites, directly occupying nasopharynx, sinuses, oropharynx or larynx.
Intellectual disability/callosal agenesis, microphthalmia and nasal hypoplasia define the syndrome; atypical oral clefting is also a defining malformation.
Central neurodegeneration causes gaze palsy, rigidity and cognitive impairment; visual and swallowing symptoms do not establish direct eye or gut damage.
Intellectual disability and strabismus define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 22/24. Hearing impairment and endocrine abnormalities are occasional.
Potassium deficiency is an electrolyte disorder; muscle symptoms and polyuria do not establish common lasting damage to those organs.
Malignancy of the tonsillar ring in the pharyngeal airway; the concept does not specify lymphoma.
SNCA-associated Parkinson disease causes central and autonomic neurodegeneration; orthostatic hypotension does not establish intrinsic cardiovascular damage.
Structural abnormality or constriction of the stomach.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the lacrimal gland, part of the ocular axis.
Enteric duplication with frequent skeletal/CNS malformations; respiratory insufficiency 80-99%. Cardiac malformations omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone does not establish damage.
Limb/vertebral, urinary and rectal dysgenesis define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia 30-79%. PDA and nail aplasia omitted by cap.
Progressive central and peripheral neurodegeneration; optic atrophy directly damages the ocular optic nerve in 4/6 patients.
Defining abnormalities affect dental enamel, ocular lenses and the cerebral aqueduct.
Congenital structural heart disease, including tetralogy of Fallot and ventricular septal defect.
Neurodevelopmental impairment in 6/6, with common spasticity and brain abnormalities; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Mandibular and facial skeletal dysostosis; supplied evidence does not establish common functional involvement of other organs.
Progressive neurologic disorder with myoclonus and ataxia in 6/6, seizures in 5/6 and cognitive deterioration in 3/6.
